title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context: Grothendieck is working out the group-theoretic description of GL(2,Z) (written GL(2,Z)^~, the variant he intends to identify with the Teichmüller group T_{1,1} of the once-punctured torus on the next page). On the previous page Corollary 1 gives an amalgamated product GL(2,Z)^~ ≅ D_ρ̃ *_{D_ω0} D_σ̃. Here D_ρ̃ = <ρ̃, τ̃'> is dihedral with ρ̃ of order 6. D_σ̃ = <σ̃, τ̃'> is dihedral with σ̃ of order 4. The common subgroup D_ω0 = <ω0, τ̃'> is a Klein four-group, embedded by ω0 ↦ ρ̃^3 and ω0 ↦ σ̃^2. In matrices, ω0 = -1. This is the classical decomposition GL(2,Z) ≅ D_12 *_{V_4} D_8 (dihedral groups of orders 12 and 8). He then picks involutive generators in each dihedral factor: r̃0 = τ̃', r̃1 = r̃0 ρ̃ (so ρ̃ = r̃0^{-1} r̃1), and r̃∞ = r̃0 σ̃^{-1}. This page states Corollary 2: GL(2,Z)^~ has a presentation with three involutive generators r̃0, r̃1, r̃∞. The relations are r̃0^2 = r̃1^2 = r̃∞^2 = 1, together with a relation between ρ̃^3 = (r̃0^{-1} r̃1)^3 and σ̃^2 = (r̃∞ r̃0^{-1})^2. Below the box something is scribbled out. In the matrix model of (29), r0 = [[0,1],[1,0]], r1 = [[-1,1],[0,1]] and r∞ = [[-1,0],[0,1]]. Then r0 r1 has trace 1 and determinant 1, so it has order 6, and r∞ r0 = [[0,-1],[1,0]] has order 4. Hence (r0 r1)^3 = (r∞ r0)^2 = -1. The correct presentation of GL(2,Z) is therefore: r_i^2 = 1, (r0 r1)^3 = (r∞ r0)^2, and the square of this common element = 1. Centrality of that element follows from the dihedral relations. If one imposes (r0 r1)^3 = (r∞ r0)^2 = 1 instead, one gets the Coxeter triangle group (2,3,∞) ≅ PGL(2,Z). The presentation serves the next section: identifying GL(2,Z) with the extended mapping class group T_{1,1} of U_{1,1} = (R/Z)^2 minus the origin, with the three reflections r0, r1, r∞ attached to the three cusps 0, 1, ∞.
errors: As transcribed, the relation reads (r̃0^{-1}r̃1)^3 = (r̃∞r̃0^{-1})^2 = 1. That presents PGL(2,Z) (the (2,3,∞) Coxeter group), not GL(2,Z). By (31)-(32), ρ̃^3 = σ̃^2 = ω0 ≠ 1, so the correct relations are (r̃0 r̃1)^3 = (r̃∞ r̃0)^2 together with ((r̃0 r̃1)^3)^2 = 1. The symbol between the two parentheses looks overwritten, and the scribbled-out line beneath may be Grothendieck's own attempt to fix this.

Notational inconsistency in the previous page's dihedral labels. D_ρ̃ has rotation of order 6 (order 12) and is called D_6, D_σ̃ has rotation of order 4 (order 8) but is called D_8, and D_ω0 (order 4) is called D_4. The convention mixes 'order of rotation' with 'order of group'.

ideas.what: Presentation of GL(2,Z) by three involutions r0, r1, r∞ (reflections associated with the cusps 0, 1, ∞), with (r0r1)^3 = (r∞r0)^2 central of order 2
ideas.modern_name: Coxeter-type presentation of GL(2,Z); central Z/2-extension of the extended modular group PGL(2,Z) ≅ triangle group (2,3,∞)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein/Fricke, Coxeter–Moser 'Generators and Relations for Discrete Groups')
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in La Longue Marche (1981); Esquisse discusses T_{1,1} and SL(2,Z) but not this presentation explicitly

ideas.what: GL(2,Z) as amalgam D_12 *_{V4} D_8 (Corollary 1, recalled here)
ideas.modern_name: Amalgam decomposition of GL(2,Z) from its action on the Bass–Serre tree
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; Serre, Trees (1977) for SL(2,Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6 and the GL analogue

deep.surprise_reason: A standard presentation of GL(2,Z) by three involutions, recorded as a step toward identifying it with T_{1,1}. As literally written it contains a slip (it would give PGL(2,Z)). Nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: The '#' superscripts on r̃0 are '-1' exponents: ρ̃ = r̃0^{-1} r̃1 and σ̃ = r̃∞ r̃0^{-1}, consistent with (33) on the previous page.
The '{+respectifs [?]+}' is better read as '(à trois générateurs involutifs r̃0, r̃1, r̃∞)'.
The symbol between (r̃0^{-1}r̃1)^3 and (r̃∞r̃0^{-1})^2 appears to be an overwritten/corrected '='. There is a crossed-out scribble beneath the box, under σ̃.
